subject: Evaluation methodology decision & ownership for BluePeak POC
messages:
From: marissa.co@redwood.com
To: Elaine Park <elaine.park@bluepeak.com>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, monica.patel@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-28T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: POC: draft success criteria + evaluation options (post-call recap)

Hi Elaine — thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth before we circle back with legal/ops.

Call summary (2 min):
- Goal: validate Redwood inference runtime for clinical note summarization at BluePeak (downstream QA reduction, latency under 250ms p50).
- Scope: small controlled POC across 3 clinics, ~2k notes/day simulated; preserve PHI controls via VPC/private test workspace.

Draft success criteria (please confirm):
1) Quality: mean Rouge-L >= 0.68 vs internal gold set (100 sampled notes) OR clinical reviewer pass-rate >= 85% on triage checklist.
2) Latency: p50 < 250ms, p95 < 1.2s for 1-2 concurrent streams.
3) Cost: per-note inference cost < $0.015 with suggested batching/quantization.
4) Security/compliance: audit-logging enabled, keys housed in customer KMS for private deployment.

Eval methodology options (we recommended two):
A) Online shadow (preferred): run Redwood in parallel on live traffic for 2 weeks; collect live errors and human-review sample. Pros: realistic distribution, faster ops validation. Cons: requires safe rollout gating and monitoring.
B) Offline evaluation: we run batched runs against curated dataset and reviewer grading. Pros: lower ops risk, reproducible. Cons: may miss live distribution shifts.

Attachments: BluePeak_POC_Draft_Outline_v1.pdf (outline, timeline, roles).

Ask: Can you confirm which eval method you prefer (Online shadow vs Offline) and whether the Quality metric should be the Rouge-L threshold or the reviewer pass-rate? If online, propose start week of Dec 7. If offline, we need the gold sample by Dec 3.

Next internal steps on our side after your confirmation: I'll loop in Steph to own the eval rubric and Rishi to be trial engineer/owner. Monica will run onboarding for CS.

Thanks — Marissa

--
Marissa Cole

From: Elaine Park <elaine.park@bluepeak.com>

Date: 2026-11-28T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: POC: draft success criteria + evaluation options (post-call recap)

Marissa — thanks for the clear notes. BluePeak prefers the Online shadow approach for this POC. A few clarifications and confirmations from our side: 

- Quality: we would prioritize clinical reviewer pass-rate >= 88% on the triage checklist (we can provide the checklist by 12/01). Rouge-L is useful but our clinicians rely on the checklist outcomes.
- Latency: p50 < 300ms is acceptable for this first pass; p95 target still useful as exploratory.
- Timeline: Dec 7 start is fine; would we expect 10 business days of shadowing (2 calendar weeks)?
- Data/ops: we'll need a scoped onboarding call with your CS team and our security folks to confirm VPC details.

Please confirm ownership and a concrete timeline for the onboarding + start of shadowing. Also share the rubric template you mentioned so our clinical QA lead can review.

Best,
Elaine
Director of Clinical Ops | BluePeak Health
elaine.park@bluepeak.com

Subject: Fwd: POC: draft success criteria + evaluation options (我要 you to own the rubric and engineer plan)

Folks — forwarding Elaine's reply. BluePeak selected Online shadow and prefers reviewer pass-rate 88% as the primary quality gate. Action items I propose: 

- Rishi: you will be the trial engineer/owner — lead onboarding, infra (VPC/keys), and runtime tuning. Deliverable: trial runbook + failure-mode checklist by 12/03.
- Steph: you own the evaluation rubric and grading flow. Please adapt the attached eval-rubric-template.xlsx to mirror BluePeak's clinical checklist; proposed columns: sample_id, clinician_id, pass/fail, severity, reviewer_notes, model_version, latency_ms. Send back by 12/02.
- Monica: lead CS onboarding call scheduling — target Fri 11/30 for a 30-min ops sync with BluePeak security.

Notes on offline vs online tradeoffs (for docs):
- Online shadow (what's needed): traffic mirroring or in-path proxy to capture inputs; KV cache warmup; partial fallback to avoid patient-impacting writes. Requires monitoring dashboards (latency, error rate, quality sampling).
- Offline: more controlled but may underrepresent edge cases (rare clinical phrasing).

Attachments: eval-rubric-template.xlsx (blank template I tailored).

Let me know if you want me to take a stab at the rubric first and then hand off; otherwise please own these dates.

Thanks — M.

- Cost target: < $0.015/note (tuning to be done during first 3 days).
